Any delays in revegetation, or barren areas resulting from adverse soil conditions, will contribute to local dust pollution problems.
Regarding human ecology, the work force must adhere to use of respirators and goggles. Such devices will help reduce health problems encountered through exposure to atmospheric dust and other industrial air pollution. Workers will, however, breath dust. The smallest dust particles will be respirable. Inhalation of the dust particles may irritate the lungs and eyes, and will make them more susceptible to infection. Low visability from heavy dust conditions will also increase the likelihood of accidents.
Economic Geology
The primary unavoidable impact on the economic geology of the region will be the depletion of the fossil fuel resource. This depletion will occur at faster rate at the high level of production (26 mtpy) than at the low level rate (19 mtpy). When the coal is mined and consumed, it cannot be replaced. The total recoverable coal resources in the lease tracts represent approximately .62% of the total U.S. economically recoverable coal reserves (CEQ, 1975). Deposits of clinker in areas to be mined will be used for surfacing of haul roads and other roads within the area of operation. Clinker not so utilized will be incorporated into mine spoils and also will be lost for possible future use.
